status_reason: The target (contaminant or quality variable) is undefined, so any method or sensor choice would rest on missing facts; an immediate exact configuration cannot be approved.
answer: An exact sensor configuration cannot be recommended yet, because the contaminant and the quality variable are not named, and for samples of incompletely known composition several optical methods must be tested first. The first step is a laboratory screen of paired in-spec and off-spec process samples, each with an independent laboratory result, starting with NIR and Raman. Only the method that separates the off-spec samples should be taken forward to a sensor configuration.

inline.headline: Test NIR first in a laboratory screen of paired in-spec and off-spec process samples, before any in-line configuration
inline.probe: NIR transmission or transflection probe for liquids (1-10 mm path), used in the laboratory first
inline.install: Not yet: the sampling point is unknown; install only after the lab screen selects the method
inline.fiber: Vis-NIR silica fiber, 350-2400 nm (covers most of the 780-2500 nm NIR range but stops short of 2500 nm)
inline.not_final_because: The contaminant and the quality variable are unknown, no calibration data exist, and NIR may lack sensitivity at low levels (bioprocess example), so the choice is provisional until paired samples are measured against laboratory references.

problems.text: An exact sensor configuration is requested before the target is known. Selecting a spectral method requires knowing the analytical problem, and for samples of unknown composition several methods are tested first, so an immediate configuration would rest on invented facts.
Contamination is only suspected and the contaminant is not named, so no method can yet be matched to it.
One method is not assumed to be enough: complex media such as oil or fermentation media may need two or more methods.

methods.why: The most common online fiber-probe method and suited to transparent liquids through transmission or transflection probes; quantitative use needs validated chemometric models.
Gives information complementary to MIR and NIR, but needs special probes and its weak signals can be masked by fluorescence.
Shows well-defined absorption peaks, but penetrates only 1-6 µm and has high cost; fiber probes need PIR fiber for the 3-16 µm range.
Highly sensitive, but it works only for substances that emit secondary light, and most chemicals do not fluoresce.

questions.q: Can you provide paired in-spec and off-spec samples, each with an independent laboratory result for the quality variable?
questions.why: Models must be built and validated on reference data before spectra can be used quantitatively.

questions.q: Where in the process is the liquid sampled, is it transparent or turbid, and what are its temperature, pressure and flow?
questions.why: Transparency decides between transmission and reflection probes, and the sampling point sets the installation.

questions.q: How often and how quickly do off-specification events occur, and can samples be taken from the process for laboratory tests?
questions.why: The AFS pathway starts with multi-method lab trials on the customer process, which needs samples.

experiment.objective: Find which quality variable or contaminant the spectra can detect, before any sensor configuration is chosen.
steps: Collect paired in-spec and off-spec process samples, each with an independent laboratory analysis; the instrument's own calibration is not used as the reference.
Measure the same samples with NIR (silica Vis-NIR fiber, transmission or transflection depending on clarity) and with Raman; add MIR ATR only if neither separates the groups.
Check whether each method sees the difference (for example by PCA), record the key spectral features, and confirm the fiber covers the measured range.
Compare the best single method with a NIR + Raman fused model on the same held-out samples, using segmented cross-validation because the data are limited.
Only after a method separates the off-spec samples, define the in-line probe, install point and calibration plan.
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client; a method is taken forward only if it separates off-spec from in-spec samples on held-out data.

pathway.key_features: Not yet identifiable; key spectral features must come from the lab screen of paired samples.
pathway.path_reason: Paths A, B and C all follow the identification of key spectral features, which cannot be done before the target is known.

multispectral.why: NIR and Raman carry complementary information (NIR sees polar groups, Raman the molecular backbone), and NIR + Raman gave the best results in an earlier pellet-coating study.
multispectral.test: Show that the fused NIR + Raman model beats the best single method on the same held-out validation samples; keep the combination only if it wins.

assumptions: The liquid is homogeneous enough that NIR and Raman can be synchronised rather than measured on the same spot; this changes if the liquid carries particles.
No sampling point, flow, temperature or distance to the spectrometer has been given.
The contaminant, if present, changes the spectra; this has not yet been shown.
The fiber range is checked for NIR only; Raman excitation and range must be checked when that method is chosen.
